question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it be community/experimental support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: The external FreeBSD port proves useful demand and a package path, but current OpenClaw does not own the docs, installer, service, CI, release, and upgrade commitments required for official support.

options.title: Define community FreeBSD scope
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide whether to acknowledge the existing FreeBSD port as community or experimental without promising Tier 1 support.

options.title: Promote toward Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing ownership and split implementation work for ports/pkg coordination, installer behavior, FreeBSD service management, docs, CI, and release validation.

options.title: Decline official support
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide the FreshPorts package should remain external and unsupported by OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Define community FreeBSD scope
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide whether to acknowledge the existing FreeBSD port as community or experimental without promising Tier 1 support.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about OpenClaw's official platform contract and roadmap scope, and CONTRIBUTING.md identifies steipete as project lead.
